mainTopic: Witnesses who cannot read or sign, documents in other languages, and doubtful cases of a גט
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא supporting רב: witnesses who cannot sign may trace their names through a paper stencil, and witnesses who cannot read may have the document read to them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits these leniencies to גיטין, and רבי אלעזר explains why: so women are not left as עגונות. After two reports of רבא's ruling, the גמרא concludes that the stencil is only for גיטין, but reading aloud is allowed for any document. Stories about רב יהודה, רב נחמן and רב פפא show when a document read by others can be trusted. אמימר rules that a Persian שטר signed by Jewish witnesses can collect even from sold property, once it meets every normal requirement. שמואל rules that a blank paper given as a גט leaves her possibly divorced, since hidden writing may appear, and רב דימי requires the witnesses to read the גט. The amud ends with cases of a supposed גט thrown among barrels and a ספר תורה handed over as a גט, and רב יוסף's discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב: a paper stencil for witnesses who cannot sign
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches רב's view. Witnesses who cannot sign are given a paper stencil, and they fill in the cut-out letters with ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same as רב: witnesses who do not know how to sign get a blank piece of paper with their names cut into it, and they fill in the cut-out spaces with ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב's ruling just discussed: witnesses who cannot write can still sign by tracing through a stencil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a witness who cannot write may sign this way. The paper is cut in the shape of his name, and he fills in the gaps with ink. The ברייתא backs up רב, so his ruling now has an earlier source behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with him (a supporting source)
The cut-out gaps in the paper

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in accordance with Rav:
Witnesses who do not know how to sign,
one tears a blank paper for them
and they fill in the gaps with ink.
phrases.notes: Think of a stencil: the letters of the name are cut out of the paper, and the witness traces them in ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling from the preceding discussion.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that witnesses who cannot sign may sign using a cut paper stencil.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that a blank paper is cut for such witnesses and they fill the gaps with ink.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the leniency to גיטין
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the stencil leniency is only for גיטין. For other documents, witnesses must know how to read and sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When does this apply? To bills of divorce. But for documents freeing slaves and all other documents, if the witnesses know how to read and sign, they sign; if not, they do not sign.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, still inside the same ברייתא, says the leniency for unskilled witnesses applies only to a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He divides documents into two groups. For גיטין, the leniency is allowed. For שחרורי עבדים and every other שטר, a witness must be able to both read and sign by himself, or he cannot sign at all.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (a phrase that limits a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as making גיטין stricter. בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים limits the leniency, so only גיטין get it. The stricter rule is for the other documents.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said? For bills of divorce of women;
but for documents freeing slaves
and all other documents,
if they know how to read and to sign, they sign,
and if not, they do not sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's leniency to גיטין only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency for unskilled witnesses applies only to גיטין. For other documents, witnesses must be able to read and sign.

steps.title: Who mentioned reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל talks about reading, when the ברייתא only discussed signing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reading — who mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל refers to reading, but the first part of the ברייתא never mentioned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא was only about witnesses who cannot sign. Yet רבן שמעון בן גמליאל speaks of witnesses who know how to read and sign, as if reading had already come up. This gap points to something missing from the text.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? (it was never brought up)

phrases.english: Reading — who mentioned its name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's mention of reading in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part of the ברייתא never discussed witnesses who cannot read, so a limit on a reading leniency seems to have nothing to refer to.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing a line about witnesses who cannot read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is incomplete. It also taught that witnesses who cannot read have the document read to them and then sign. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits both leniencies to גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something is missing, and this is what it teaches: Witnesses who cannot read have the document read to them and they sign. Witnesses who cannot sign use the stencil, and so on. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When does this apply? To bills of divorce. But for documents freeing slaves and all other documents, if they know how to read and sign, they sign; if not, they do not sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in a missing line at the start of the ברייתא about witnesses who cannot read. Then it repeats the whole ברייתא in its corrected form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we add the line that a document is read aloud to witnesses who cannot read, there are two leniencies: one for reading and one for signing. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits both of them to גיטין. That explains why he speaks of reading and signing together.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing from the text
And this is what it teaches
One reads the document in front of them

steps.whatToRemember: With the missing line added, the ברייתא has two leniencies for גיטין: reading the document to witnesses who cannot read, and a stencil for witnesses who cannot sign. For other documents, neither leniency applies.

phrases.english: It is missing something,
and this is what it teaches:
Witnesses who do not know how to read —
one reads in front of them and they sign,
and those who do not know how to sign, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points back to the stencil rule from the start of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said? For bills of divorce of women;
but documents freeing slaves
and all other documents,
if they know how to read and to sign, they sign,
and if not, they do not sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by adding the missing line about reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא: the text is missing a line, which the גמרא fills in
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא only discussed signing, so the mention of reading seemed out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא also taught a leniency for witnesses who cannot read. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits both leniencies to גיטין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the reason is to prevent עגונות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient only for גיטין: so that Jewish women are not left unable to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? So that the daughters of Israel should not be left as עגונות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks and answers why גיטין get a leniency that other documents do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גט needed witnesses who can read and write, a husband might not find such witnesses. He could then leave without giving the גט, and his wife would be stuck, unable to remarry. To prevent this, the חכמים were lenient for גיטין, but not for other documents.

keyTerms.meaning: Women left stuck in their marriage, unable to remarry

steps.whyThisMatters: Preventing עגונות is a major reason for leniency in the laws of גיטין. It explains why a גט can be treated differently from other documents.
steps.whatToRemember: גיטין get special leniencies about witnesses because of the concern for עגונות. Other documents have no such concern, so they keep the regular strict rule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
So that the daughters of Israel should not be deserted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's distinction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיטין are treated leniently so that women are not left as עגונות.

steps.title: Two reports of רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but רב גמדא reports in רבא's name that the הלכה is not like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But רב גמדא said in רבא's name: the הלכה does not follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opposite reports of what רבא ruled about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first report, the stencil and read-aloud leniencies apply only to גיטין. In the second report, the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which seems to mean it follows the רבנן, who allow these leniencies for all documents.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
And Rav Gamda said in the name of Rava:
The halacha is not like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the dispute between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן explained in steps 2-5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are conflicting reports of רבא: the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, or it is not.

steps.title: How can the הלכה follow the רבנן when רב כהנא punished this?
steps.stepSummary: If the הלכה follows the רבנן, why did רב כהנא have someone flogged for using the stencil on other documents?
steps.simpleTranslation: If not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, then like whom? Like the רבנן? But there was a man who used the stencil method for other documents, and רב כהנא had him flogged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב גמדא's report. A real case showed that using the stencil on regular documents was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the הלכה follows the רבנן, a stencil would be fine for any document. But רב כהנא had a man punished for doing exactly that. This suggests the הלכה does follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, at least for the stencil.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual case, a real-life act

phrases.english: Then like whom? Like the Rabbis?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָהוּא דַּעֲבַד עוֹבָדָא בִּשְׁאָר שְׁטָרוֹת,
phrases.english: But there was a certain man who acted this way with other documents,
phrases.notes: He means he let witnesses trace their names with the stencil from step 1.

phrases.english: and Rav Kahana had him flogged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב גמדא's version of רבא's ruling from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גמדא's report that the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling like the רבנן allows the stencil for all documents, yet רב כהנא punished someone for doing that with regular documents.

steps.title: The ruling was only about reading
steps.stepSummary: רב גמדא's report was only about reading to the witnesses, not about the stencil.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explained it as talking only about reading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב גמדא's version of רבא only applied to the read-aloud leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For reading, the הלכה follows the רבנן, so any document may be read to a witness who cannot read. For the stencil, the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and allows it only for גיטין. That is why רב כהנא punished the man.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, he interpreted it
Reading, here the document being read aloud to the witness

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the stencil is allowed only for גיטין, but a witness who cannot read may have any document read to him.
steps.confusionAlert: Both reports of רבא can be true at once. One is about the stencil, and the other is about reading.

phrases.english: He explained it as referring to reading.
phrases.notes: The two leniencies come from step 4. Only the reading one follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב גמדא's report rejects רבן שמעון בן גמליאל for both leniencies, including the stencil.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב גמדא's report rejects רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for reading. For the stencil, the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: עולא tells רב יהודה he may have documents read to him
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה struggled to read before signing. עולא told him this was unnecessary, because רבי אלעזר and רב נחמן had documents read to them and then signed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה would struggle to read and then sign. עולא told him: you don't need to. רבי אלעזר, the master of ארץ ישראל, had documents read before him and signed. And the court scribes read documents before רב נחמן, and he signed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts the read-aloud leniency into practice. עולא tells רב יהודה that great רבנים relied on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the ruling in step 8: reading a document to the signer is allowed even for regular documents. עולא brings two great authorities as proof that רב יהודה does not need to strain himself.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would struggle to read and then sign.
Ulla said to him: You don't need to,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מָרָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: for Rabbi Elazar, the master of Eretz Yisrael,
they would read before him and he would sign,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן – קָרוּ קַמֵּיהּ סָפְרֵי דַּיָּינֵי וְחָתֵים.
phrases.english: and Rav Nachman, the court scribes would read before him and he would sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the read-aloud leniency from step 8 being used in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A signer may have a document read to him instead of reading it himself, as רבי אלעזר and רב נחמן did.

steps.title: The leniency works only when the readers fear the signer
steps.stepSummary: Reading aloud was trusted only because רב נחמן's court scribes were in awe of him. With other scribes, or with someone other than רב נחמן, it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to רב נחמן and the court scribes, because they were in awe of him. But רב נחמן with other scribes, or the court scribes with another person, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the precedent of רב נחמן to a specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court scribes worked under רב נחמן and feared him, so they would not dare read the document falsely. Without that relationship, there is a worry the reader might misread on purpose. Then the leniency does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: Having a document read to you is valid only when the reader is someone who would not dare to lie to you.

phrases.english: And this is specifically Rav Nachman and the court scribes,
since they have fear of him,
but Rav Nachman with other scribes,
or the court scribes with another person, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the precedent of רב נחמן cited in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading to a signer is trusted only when the readers are in awe of him, like court scribes before their judge.

steps.title: רב פפא and Persian documents from non-Jewish courts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא had two non-Jews read a Persian document, each separately and casually. Then he would collect with it, even from property that had been sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a Persian document made in non-Jewish courts came before רב פפא, he had two non-Jews read it, each one without the other present, speaking casually. Then he would collect with it even from sold property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story of having a document read aloud. This time רב פפא could not read the language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew cannot be a formal witness. But when he speaks casually, without knowing his words matter, he is believed. Using two readers separately makes sure they agree on what is written. Once the contents were clear, רב פפא treated the document as fully valid, even for collecting from sold property.

keyTerms.meaning: Speaking casually, without knowing he is testifying
Property that was sold but is still bound to a loan

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a document you cannot read yourself can still be used, if there is a reliable way to know what it says.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא, כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי לְקַמֵּיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa, when there would come before him

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטָרָא פָּרְסָאָה דַּעֲבִיד בְּעַרְכָּאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: a Persian document that was made in non-Jewish courts,
would have two non-Jews read it
one not in the presence of the other
speaking casually, without intent to testify,
and he would collect with it even from sold property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא, כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי לְקַמֵּיהּ שְׁטָרָא פָּרְסָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of relying on others to read a document, with safeguards against misreading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Persian document from a non-Jewish court may be read by two non-Jews separately and casually. Then it can be used to collect even from sold property.

steps.title: A Persian document signed by Jewish witnesses can collect from sold property
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that a Persian-language שטר signed by Jewish witnesses is fully valid, even for collecting from sold property (משעבדי).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רב הונא בר נתן told me that אמימר said: A Persian document signed by Jewish witnesses can be used to collect a debt, even from property the borrower already sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from אמימר: a Persian-language loan document signed by Jewish witnesses is good enough to collect even from sold property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting from sold property (משעבדי) is the strongest power a שטר can have, so this is a big statement. The document is in Persian, but the witnesses are Jewish. The next steps will test whether such a document can really work.

keyTerms.meaning: Property tied to the debt that the borrower later sold

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן,
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Natan said to me,
so said Ameimar:
This Persian document
on which Jewish witnesses are signed,
we collect with it even from sold property.
phrases.notes: Land the borrower sold after taking the loan. The lender can take it back from the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אָמַר לִי רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן, הָכִי אָמַר אַמֵּימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of non-Jewish or foreign-language documents from רב פפא's practice in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Persian שטר with Jewish witnesses can collect even from משעבדי.

steps.title: The witnesses cannot read Persian
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: Jewish witnesses usually can't read Persian, so how can they sign it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they don't know how to read it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר: how can witnesses sign a document they cannot read?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses must know what they are signing. Most Jews could not read Persian, so their signatures would seem to mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They don't know how to read

phrases.english: But they don't know how to read it!
phrases.notes: "They" means the Jewish witnesses, who usually couldn't read Persian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's ruling from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's validation of the Persian שטר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses who can't read the document can't truly testify to what it says.

steps.title: The witnesses can read Persian
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies when the witnesses do know how to read Persian.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's talking about witnesses who do know how to read it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case to witnesses who can read Persian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not thrown out. It is limited to a case where the problem doesn't exist.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where they know

phrases.english: It's when they do know how.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reading challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling covers any Jewish witnesses, even ones who can't read Persian.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling covers only witnesses who can read Persian.

steps.title: A document must be written so it can't be forged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a שטר must be written in a way that can't be forged, and Persian documents aren't.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we require writing that cannot be forged, and this doesn't have it!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge: Persian documents were not protected against tampering, and every valid שטר must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan document that could easily be changed can't be trusted to take someone's property. So even with readable text, the document seems invalid.

phrases.english: But we require writing
that cannot be forged,
and this doesn't have it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעֵינַן כְּתָב שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהִזְדַּיֵּיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new problem with אמימר's ruling, after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's validation of the Persian שטר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every שטר must be safe from forgery, and Persian documents are not.

steps.title: The paper was treated with gall
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies when the paper was treated with gall, so the writing can't be changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's a case where the paper was treated with gall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by again narrowing the case: the paper was treated so the ink can't be erased and rewritten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the paper is treated with gall, the forgery problem is gone. So the document meets the normal requirement.

phrases.english: When the paper was treated with gall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the forgery challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any Persian document would be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a Persian document on gall-treated paper is valid.

steps.title: A document must repeat its main point in the last line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a שטר must restate its main content in the last line, and Persian documents don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we require that the document repeat its main content in the last line, and this doesn't have it!
steps.whatsHappening: A third challenge: a proper שטר ends with a line summarizing its content, and Persian documents don't do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closing summary line protects the document from things being added in empty space above the signatures. Without it, the document would seem invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: To restate the document's main content

phrases.english: But we require
"One must repeat the main content of the document
in the last line,"
and this doesn't have it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעֵינַן צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר מֵעִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר בְּשִׁיטָה אַחֲרוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third problem with אמימר's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's validation of the Persian שטר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A valid שטר must restate its content in the last line, and Persian documents lack this.

steps.title: The document does repeat its main point
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies when the Persian document does restate its content in the last line.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's a case where it does repeat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers once more by narrowing the case: this Persian document does have the summary line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now all three problems are solved. אמימר's ruling is about a Persian document that meets every normal requirement of a שטר.

phrases.english: When it does repeat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the summary-line challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Persian documents without a summary line would be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a Persian document with the summary line is valid.

steps.title: What is new? A משנה already allows any language
steps.stepSummary: If the document meets every requirement, אמימר only teaches that any language is fine. But a משנה already says a גט in Hebrew or Greek is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: So then what is he teaching us, that every language is valid? We already learned this: A גט written in Hebrew with its witnesses signed in Greek, or written in Greek with its witnesses signed in Hebrew, is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: After all the conditions, the גמרא asks what אמימר is adding. It seems to be the same thing a משנה already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With every problem removed, the only thing left is the language itself. A משנה already says language doesn't matter, so אמימר's statement looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: But then what is he teaching us —
that every language is valid?!
We already learned it:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in מסכת גיטין (87b).

phrases.english: A bill of divorce written in Hebrew
with its witnesses signed in Greek,
or in Greek with its witnesses in Hebrew —
it is valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the conditions of steps 14-18, asks what new point is left in אמימר's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already says a document in any language is valid, so אמימר adds nothing.

steps.title: Without אמימר, we would limit the rule to גיטין
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we might think the rule is only for a גט. אמימר teaches it applies to all documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that משנה, I would have said: this applies only to a גט, but not to other documents. So אמימר teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אמימר is needed, because the משנה only talks about a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think a גט gets a special leniency, so that a woman can remarry. אמימר shows that any language is valid for loan documents too, even for collecting from sold property.
steps.whatToRemember: A Persian שטר signed by Jewish witnesses is valid, even against sold property, if the witnesses can read it, the paper can't be forged, and the last line restates the content. אמימר's חידוש is that any language works for all documents, not just a גט.
steps.confusionAlert: The language was never the real problem. The three challenges were about reading, forgery, and the summary line, and each was solved by narrowing the case.

phrases.english: If we only had that source,
I would have said:
this applies only to bills of divorce,
but for other documents — no,
so he teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the "what's new" challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point beyond the earlier source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any language is valid only for a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any language is valid for all documents, including loan documents.

steps.title: A blank paper given as a divorce document
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a woman handed a blank paper as her גט is divorced, out of concern that it was written with מי מילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If a man gave his wife a blank piece of paper and told her, 'This is your גט,' she is divorced. We worry that maybe he wrote it with מי מילין, and the writing has disappeared into the paper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from שמואל about a גט that looks completely blank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some liquids leave writing that later sinks into the paper and can no longer be seen. Since the paper might once have held a real גט, שמואל will not simply ignore it. The woman is treated as divorced because of this possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned (we take the possibility seriously)
Gall water, a liquid whose writing can sink into paper and vanish

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the word חיישינן in mind. It turns out to be the key to the whole discussion at the end.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
If he gave her a blank piece of paper,
and said to her: "This is your bill of divorce" –
she is divorced;
we are concerned that perhaps he wrote it with gall water.
phrases.notes: Writing done with this liquid can sink into the paper, so the paper only looks blank now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from אמימר's ruling about documents in other languages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blank paper handed over as a גט leaves her divorced, since it may have been written with מי מילין.

steps.title: A teaching about a document that was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a woman destroyed a paper called a גט, and the husband then claimed it was a different kind of document. She is still divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: A husband said, 'This is your גט.' She took it and threw it into the sea, into a fire, or anywhere it would be destroyed. Then he said, 'It was really a שטר פסים' or 'It was a שטר אמנה.' She is divorced, and he does not have the power to forbid her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל. This step only quotes the source. The actual point against שמואל comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the husband called the paper a גט, and it was destroyed before anyone could check it. His later claim that it was only a fake loan document is not believed, so she stays divorced. The details of this case will be used to draw an inference.

keyTerms.meaning: A display document, a fake loan note to make someone look wealthy
A trust document, a loan note written before any loan was given
To make her forbidden (as still married)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"This is your bill of divorce";
and she took it and threw it into the sea,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לָאוּר, אוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר הָאָבֵד;
phrases.english: or into the fire, or into anything that destroys it;
and he later said:
"It is a display document,"
"It is a document of trust" –
she is divorced,
and he does not have the power to make her forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source in order to challenge שמואל's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a blank paper can count as a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the ברייתא, whose wording will show that writing is required.

steps.title: Writing is needed, but שמואל's paper has none
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא the גמרא infers that she is divorced only because the paper had writing, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason she is divorced is that the paper had writing on it. But if it had no writing, she would not be divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the inference from the ברייתא that forms the real attack on שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, we worry the destroyed paper was a real גט only because it had writing we can no longer check. That suggests a paper with no writing at all is not a גט. This is exactly שמואל's case, yet he said she is divorced.

phrases.english: The reason is that there is writing,
but if there is no writing – no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by drawing an inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a blank paper divorces her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that without visible writing there is no divorce, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל means a paper tested with colored liquid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's case is one where the paper is tested with a colored liquid. If hidden writing comes out, she is divorced. If not, the paper means nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל said this, he meant a case where we test the paper with a colored liquid. If the paper brings out writing, then it brings it out and counts. If it does not, the paper is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing שמואל's ruling to a paper that has been tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל never said that any blank paper divorces her. A test can show whether hidden writing is in the paper. Only if writing appears is she divorced, so his ruling fits the ברייתא's need for writing.

keyTerms.meaning: A colored liquid used to bring out hidden writing
It is nothing (it has no legal meaning)

phrases.english: When Shmuel said it,
it was where we check it with a colored liquid;
if it expels the writing – it expels it,
phrases.notes: Meaning the hidden letters show up, so it counts as a written גט.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא פָּלֵיט – לָאו כְּלוּם הוּא.
phrases.english: and if it does not expel it – it is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to say that a completely blank paper divorces her with no checking.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל refers to a paper tested with colored liquid that brings out writing, so writing is still required.

steps.title: Writing that appears only now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even if the test brings out writing, maybe the writing became visible only now and was not readable when he gave it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it does bring out writing, so what? It is only now that the writing comes out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be valid at the moment it is handed over. When he gave it, the paper looked blank. Writing that shows up only after the test may not prove there was a proper גט at the time of giving.

phrases.english: And if it expels the writing, what of it?
It is only now that it expels it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the colored-liquid test makes the blank paper a valid גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The writing became visible only after the test, not when the גט was given, so it should not make her definitely divorced.

steps.title: שמואל only said 'we are concerned'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל never called her definitely divorced. He said חיישינן, so she is only possibly divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל too only said, 'We are concerned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last objection by pointing back to שמואל's exact word, חיישינן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is correct that writing appearing now does not prove a valid גט back then. But שמואל agrees. He only meant that we cannot ignore the possibility, so she is in a state of doubt. She is not free to remarry as fully divorced, and she is also not treated as simply still married.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's blank-paper ruling applies only when a test brings out hidden writing. Even then she is only possibly divorced (חיישינן), not definitely divorced.

phrases.english: Shmuel too,
said only "we are concerned."
phrases.notes: Look back at his words in step 21. He never said she is definitely divorced, only that we worry she might be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 25 by rereading שמואל's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's 'she is divorced' seemed to mean a certain divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל said חיישינן, so the divorce is only a doubt, which fits the concern that the writing appeared only now.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one word in a מימרא, חיישינן, can turn what looks like a clear ruling into a ruling of doubt.

steps.title: Witnesses must read the גט
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports, in a chain going back to רב דימי, that the two witnesses who watch a גט being given must read it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: אמימר told me that מרימר said in the name of רב דימי: the two witnesses in front of whom the גט is given need to read it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: the witnesses who watch the husband give the גט must read it, not just see a paper being handed over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about a paper whose writing could not be checked. Here רב דימי adds a requirement. The witnesses must actually read the גט, so they know it really is a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: two people, meaning the two witnesses

phrases.english: Ravina said: Ameimar said to me,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר מָרִימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי:
phrases.english: so said Mareimar in the name of Rav Dimi:
these two witnesses
in front of whom he gives the bill of divorce
need to read it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אֲמַר לִי אַמֵּימָר, הָכִי אָמַר מָרִימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: what the witnesses must do when a גט is handed over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two witnesses to the handing over of a גט must read it.

steps.title: Challenge from the woman who destroyed her גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again. The husband's claim that the paper was a different document is rejected. If the witnesses had read the paper, why would anyone even think his claim could work?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: "Here is your גט." She took it and threw it into the sea, or into fire, or into anything that destroys it. Then he said, "It was a document of appeasement" or "It was a document of trust." She is divorced, and he cannot make her forbidden. If the witnesses must read it, then after they read it, how could he even say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב דימי using the same ברייתא it quoted earlier in step 22, but now for a new reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses read the גט, everyone already knows it was a real גט. So the husband's claim is plainly false, and the ברייתא would have no reason to tell us that his claim does not work. The ברייתא seems to describe a case where the witnesses did not read it, which goes against רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: to make her forbidden to other men

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא as in step 22, but now it is used against רב דימי, not against שמואל.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"This is your bill of divorce";
and she took it and threw it into the sea,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לָאוּר, אוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר הָאָבֵד;
phrases.english: or into the fire, or into anything that destroys it;
and he then said: "It is a document of appeasement,"
"It is a document of trust" –
she is divorced,
and he does not have the power to make her forbidden.
And if you say they need to read it,
after they read it,
is he able to say this to her?!
phrases.notes: The witnesses already saw that it was a גט, so his claim is obviously false. Why would the ברייתא need to tell us that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's rule from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's rule that the witnesses must read the גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the witnesses read it, the husband's claim is obviously false, so the ברייתא's ruling would be pointless.

steps.title: He hid it under his arm after they read it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a case where the husband took the גט under his arm after it was read and then took it out. We might have worried that he switched it, and the ברייתא teaches that we do not worry about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where, after they read it, he put it under his arm and took it out again. You might have said he switched it. The ברייתא teaches us that he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains a case where the husband's claim does sound possible, even though the witnesses read the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did read it, but then it was out of sight for a moment. So the husband could claim he swapped it for a different paper. The ברייתא teaches that we ignore that claim, so it does teach something new, and רב דימי stands.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for this case

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where, after they read it,
he put it under his arm and took it out,
you might have said: he switched it,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the גט was out of sight, we might think he switched it.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry that he switched it. She is divorced, and רב דימי's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The witnesses must read the גט. If the husband hid it for a moment afterward, we do not believe him if he says he switched it.

steps.title: A גט thrown among barrels, and only a מזוזה was found
steps.stepSummary: A man threw what he called a גט among the barrels, but only a מזוזה was found there. רב נחמן says a מזוזה is not usually among barrels, so the man must have thrown the מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man threw a גט to his wife among the barrels, and a מזוזה was found. רב נחמן said: a מזוזה among the barrels is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story and gives רב נחמן's ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a real גט was thrown and lost, while the מזוזה just happened to be there. רב נחמן reasons that a מזוזה is not usually found among barrels. So the paper that was found is the one he threw, and there was no גט.

keyTerms.meaning: a certain man, used to open a story

phrases.english: A certain man who threw a bill of divorce
to his wife among the barrels,
and a mezuza was found.
Rav Nachman said:
A mezuza among the barrels is not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּזְרַק לָהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about a גט that may have been lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since a מזוזה is not usually among barrels, we assume he threw the מזוזה, and she is not divorced.

steps.title: Only if one מזוזה was found
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's ruling applies only when one מזוזה was found. If two or three were found, they were probably there before, so we say the גט was taken by mice.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when one was found. But if two or three were found, then just as this one was there before, that one was also there. As for the גט, say mice took it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב נחמן's ruling to a case where only one מזוזה was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If several מזוזות are there, this place clearly holds מזוזות, so finding one proves nothing about what he threw. Then the גט may really have been thrown and carried off by mice, so she is treated as divorced.

phrases.english: And this applies only where one was found,
but if two or three were found –
since this one was there, this one too was there;
and the bill of divorce – say that mice took it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב נחמן's ruling from step 30.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With one מזוזה found, there was no גט. With two or three found, we assume the מזוזות were already there and mice took the גט.
steps.whatToRemember: How much we can learn from what was found depends on what is usually in that place: one מזוזה among barrels is unusual, but several show that מזוזות belong there.

steps.title: A man gives his wife a ספר תורה and calls it her גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story: a man went into a בית כנסת, took a ספר תורה, gave it to his wife, and said, "Here is your גט."
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain man who went into a בית כנסת, took a ספר תורה, gave it to his wife, and said to her: "Here is your גט."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new real-life case to set up the next discussion. It does not give a ruling yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last case was about a man who threw a supposed גט among barrels. This new case also involves a man who called something a גט, but here the object is clearly a ספר תורה. The question is whether we must worry that she is now divorced.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who entered the synagogue,
took a Torah scroll,
gave it to his wife,
and said to her: Here is your divorce document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case, similar in theme to the barrels case in steps 30-31. In both, a man calls an object a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The step only presents the case of a ספר תורה handed over as a גט.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what there is to worry about
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף opens his ruling by asking what concern there could possibly be in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is there to worry about here?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts answering the case with a question that hints there is nothing to worry about. He is setting up a list of possible worries that he will knock down one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not really asking for information. It is a way of saying "I don't see any problem." He then goes through each possible reason someone might think this works as a גט.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
For what is there to be concerned for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לְמַאי לֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the case in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף's position, hinted here: there is no real reason to worry that this was a valid גט.

steps.title: Rejecting the worry about hidden writing in gall water
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the first possible worry. Someone might think a גט was written on the parchment in מי מילין and can no longer be seen. But writing in מי מילין does not last on top of מי מילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you are worried because of gall water, gall water does not last on top of gall water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings up the first possible worry and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the man wrote a גט on the scroll's parchment in מי מילין, and the writing has since faded out of sight. רב יוסף answers that the parchment itself was already treated with מי מילין. So new writing in מי מילין would not last on it, and we need not worry that such a hidden גט exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Gall water, a liquid used for writing and used to treat parchment

phrases.english: If it is because of gall water,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מֵי מֵילִין עַל גַּבֵּי מֵי מֵילִין;
phrases.english: gall water does not last on top of gall water;
phrases.notes: The parchment of a ספר תורה was already treated with gall water, so new gall-water writing will not stay on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins going through the possible worries raised by the question in step 33.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the first possible worry, about hidden gall-water writing. Other worries may still follow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Writing in מי מילין cannot last on parchment that was already treated with מי מילין, so no hidden גט could be there.
